claims.text: The target system includes high-entropy carbonitrides (TiZrTaHfNb)C_xN_1-x in crystalline and liquid states near 3500 K.
The proposed method is generally applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys, especially refractory systems, near their melting temperatures.
A DNN potential should replace a conventional EAM potential as the reference model for thermodynamic integration.
The DNN potential is trained through active learning using configurations originating from AIMD calculations.
The training ensemble broadly covers relevant atomic configurations.
The DNN has a many-body representation that more accurately captures the configurational diversity of the liquid.
Iterative training on AIMD or DFT data enables the DNN to learn a more complete representation of the ab initio energy landscape.
The learned representation improves reference–target phase-space overlap in the ab initio liquid.
The improved phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Conventional TOR-TILD EAM references inadequately represent the configurational diversity of the ab initio liquid.
The DNN intervention will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by several tens of percent.
Reduced path mismatch will produce more accurate free-energy estimates.
An actively learned DeepMD potential can be used to calculate heating and cooling curves, melting hysteresis, and melting temperatures for (TiZrTaHfNb)C_xN_1-x.
The approach covers high-entropy carbonitrides with different levels of carbon-to-nitrogen substitution.
The method may be less effective when high-quality AIMD training data are sparse or at temperatures far from the training or melting regime.
Performance may not transfer reliably to alloys whose bonding differs substantially from that of the trained system.
A failure to achieve a statistically significant improvement or more than a 20% reduction in path mismatch relative to the EAM control is proposed as a falsification criterion.
